tldr: MAgIC introduces a competition-based benchmark evaluating 7 LLMs across 5 multi-agent scenarios using 7 quantitative metrics, revealing a threefold capability gap between top and bottom models, and demonstrating that PGM enhancement improves all tested models by an average of 37%.
contributions: A competition-based benchmark with 100+ cases across 5 scenarios (2 social deduction games: Chameleon, Undercover; 3 game theory scenarios: Cost Sharing, Multi-turn Prisoner's Dilemma, Public Good) and 7 metrics measuring cognition, adaptability, rationality, and collaboration
Evaluation of 7 LLMs (GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4, GPT-4-turbo, GPT-o1, Llama-2-70B, PaLM 2, Claude 2, Cohere) showing GPT-o1 as strongest and Llama-2-70B as weakest with over threefold gap
A PGM-aware agent integrating Probabilistic Graphical Models with LLMs via a two-hop Theory of Mind mechanism, boosting abilities by 37% on average
methods: The authors constructed a competition-based evaluation where challenger LLMs face a fixed defender (GPT-4) across social deduction and game theory scenarios. Seven metrics were defined: Judgment (correct vote ratio), Reasoning (multi-hop logical analysis), Self-awareness (role identification), Deception (successful misdirection), Cooperation (collective efficacy in cost-sharing), Coordination (facilitating agreement), and Rationality (optimizing self-interest). They further designed a PGM-aware agent that uses a two-hop understanding mechanism—analyzing both its own and others' perspectives—via probabilistic graphical models with random variables B1, B2, B3 representing interpretations from each player's viewpoint, conditioned on game context T_i-1.
results: GPT-4-turbo achieved the highest win rate at 57.2%, followed by GPT-4 at 53.3%. GPT-o1 excelled in Judgment, Self-awareness, Cooperation, and Coordination. GPT-4 scored 90% in Judgment and 75.0% in Deception. GPT-4-turbo surpassed Llama-2-70B by more than threefold in overall multi-agent capabilities. PGM enhancement improved all tested models by an average of 37%. The benchmark showed that metric area sizes correlated directly with winning rates, validating the evaluation framework.
limitations: The paper appears truncated, limiting full visibility into reported limitations. The competition uses only GPT-4 as the fixed defender, which may introduce bias. Some scenarios (e.g., cost guessing in Chameleon) were downweighted with λ=0.25 due to not all games triggering code guesses, potentially underrepresenting certain deception scenarios.
